items.text: Intersection of two affines need not be affine
$X=\mathbf E^n_S$, $n\ge2$, $U=X\setminus(\text{zero section})$ is not affine ($n=1$: affine).
Glue $X_1$, $X_2$ (copies of $X$) along $U$: $X_1\cap X_2=U$, both $X_i$ affine open, $U$ not affine.
Quasi-separated

$f\colon X\to S$ quasi-separated: the diagonal $\Delta_f$ is quasi-compact; i.e. after any base change every section is quasi-compact; i.e. $\ker(u,v)\to Y$ quasi-compact for all $u,v\colon Y\rightrightarrows X$.
Separated $\Rightarrow$ quasi-separated; monomorphisms and diagonals are quasi-separated; $g\circ f$ quasi-separated $\Rightarrow$ $f$ quasi-separated.
Absolute: quasi-separated over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$, i.e. $X\to X\times X$ quasi-compact. Absolute $\Rightarrow$ relative over any $S$; for $S$ quasi-separated the two notions agree.
Topologically: $X$ quasi-separated $\iff$ the intersection of two quasi-compact opens is quasi-compact.
Equivalent forms for S
$S$ quasi-separated $\iff$ every morphism $X\to S$ with $X$ quasi-compact is quasi-compact
$\iff$ for $X,Y$ quasi-compact over $S$, $X\times_S Y$ is quasi-compact.
X\times_S Y=(X\times Y)\times_{S\times S}S,\qquad X\times_S Y\to X\times Y\ \text{quasi-compact (base change of }\Delta_S)
Conversely, $S=\bigcup S_i$ quasi-compact opens: $S$ quasi-separated $\iff$ all $S_i\cap S_j$ are quasi-compact.
Counterexample: not quasi-separated
$Z=\operatorname{Spec}k[t_1,t_2,\dots]$, $U=Z\setminus\{0\}$ is not quasi-compact (the ideal $(t_i)_i$ is not generated by finitely many elements up to radical).
Glue two copies of $Z$ along $U$: two affine opens whose intersection $U$ is not quasi-compact.
Converses
$\Delta_g$ is an immersion, locally of finite type; if quasi-compact then of finite type.
$g\circ f$ quasi-compact and $g$ quasi-separated $\Rightarrow$ $f$ quasi-compact; $g\circ f$ of finite type and $g$ quasi-separated $\Rightarrow$ $f$ of finite type.
Coherent morphisms
Coherent = quasi-compact and quasi-separated: both $f$ and $\Delta_f$ are quasi-compact.
Stable under base change and composition. $g\circ f$ coherent and $g$ quasi-separated $\Rightarrow$ $f$ coherent.
A scheme is coherent if coherent over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ (quasi-compact and quasi-separated); over a quasi-separated $S$, $X$ coherent $\iff$ $X\to S$ coherent.
Direct images
$f\colon X\to S$ coherent, $\mathcal F$ quasi-coherent on $X$ $\Rightarrow$ $f_*\mathcal F$ quasi-coherent (and the higher direct images $R^if_*\mathcal F$).
